prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.15
  tan: 0.85
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
Summary of the 2010 manifesto (policies only, with ideological framing removed)

- Defence and security
  - End involvement in Afghanistan; avoid conflict with Iran.
  - Withdraw troops from Germany; renegotiate NATO terms.
  - Increase defence spending by inflation +1% for five years; maintain an independent nuclear deterrent; strengthen the Navy; restore historic regiments.
  - Introduce a compulsory one-year community service scheme for school leavers.

- Immigration, asylum, and borders
  - Halt most new immigration, with limited work and study exceptions.
  - Deport illegal immigrants and foreign nationals convicted of crimes; impose lifetime re‑entry bans for immigration law violations.
  - End asylum claims not made in the first safe country; no amnesties.
  - Incentivise voluntary resettlement; expand border control capacity.
  - Review citizenship grants since 1997.
  - Halt immigration from Muslim‑majority countries; deport radical Islamist preachers and attendees at their sermons.
  - Repeal race/equalities legislation; restrict multilingual official documents to UK indigenous languages.

- European Union and foreign policy
  - Withdraw immediately from the EU; oppose the euro; negotiate independent trade deals; redirect membership costs to domestic needs.
  - Adopt a non‑interventionist foreign policy; end foreign aid and link any assistance to resettlement aims.

- Constitution, law, and civil liberties
  - Create an English parliament; form a pan‑British parliament for shared matters; reform the House of Lords with non‑party experts.
  - Introduce citizens’ initiative referenda; a new Bill of Rights; recall of MPs; updated treason laws.
  - Restrict postal voting; forbid third‑party election interventions.
  - Repeal the Human Rights Act; withdraw from the ECHR; oppose ID cards and surveillance laws.

- Media and democracy
  - Criminal liability for knowingly false reporting; independent complaints body with right of reply and compensation.

- Culture and civil society
  - Emphasise traditional civility in schools and services; expand teaching of national history and culture.
  - Support high streets (levy on large supermarkets) and protect pubs (tax relief, supervised smoking rooms, lower pub alcohol duty); add patron‑saint bank holidays.

- Crime and justice
  - Refocus policing on crime prevention; reduce bureaucracy.
  - Reintroduce corporal punishment and capital punishment for specified offences.
  - Strengthen householders’ self‑defence rights; ensure full sentence service; expand drug rehabilitation.
  - Establish a remote penal facility for repeat violent offenders; require prison work programmes.

- Health
  - Protect a free NHS; clear deficits by reallocating foreign aid; cut bureaucracy; oppose PFI.
  - Curb “health tourism”; prioritise domestic recruitment; restore ward‑based cleaning; keep local hospitals.

- Education
  - Restore traditional curricula, A/O‑levels, streaming, grammar schools, competitive sport.
  - Expand apprenticeships; subsidise STEM; free university for those completing community service; reopen special needs schools; daily assemblies on traditional values.

- Transport
  - Reverse rail privatisation; invest in high‑speed maglev; reopen lines; upgrade waterways.
  - Replace vehicle excise duty with fuel‑based funding; reduce fuel tax burden; raise motorway speed limit to 90 mph; charge foreign trucks.

- Agriculture and fisheries
  - Replace CAP with a UK system; support family farms; ban GM crops; soil renewal; encourage organic methods.
  - Ban non‑stunned ritual slaughter.
  - Restore a 200‑mile exclusive fishing zone; enhance conservation.

- Energy
  - Expand nuclear power under British ownership; modern clean‑coal; oppose wind expansion and carbon‑credit schemes; fund wave/hydrogen research.

- Economy and tax
  - Cut spending on EU costs, foreign aid, climate programmes, overseas wars, immigration/asylum, and quangos; protect frontline services.
  - Raise personal allowance to £12,500; reintroduce a married allowance; lift inheritance tax threshold to £1m; cut council tax via programme reductions.
  - Separate retail and investment banking; strengthen capital rules; curb bonus culture; review PFI; oppose privatising natural monopolies (e.g., post, rail).
  - Vet foreign takeovers for national/public interest; apply selective tariffs tied to labour and environmental standards; ease regulation on SMEs; support co‑ops; consider limited sovereign money issuance.

- Local economies
  - Expand autonomous credit unions; explore voluntary local currencies.

- Pensions and care
  - Raise state pension to £150/week and link to earnings; gradually raise retirement age; tighten eligibility to citizens and full contributors; reduce the annual tax‑relief cap on pension contributions; oppose any EU‑wide pension bailouts; end forced home sales for care.

- IT and digital
  - Invest in technology universities; protect local IT jobs; nationalise telecoms infrastructure to deliver universal 100 Mbps broadband.
  - Guarantee personal data access rights; target uploaders in anti‑piracy enforcement; scrap national ID database.

TEXT_D:
Summary (max 500 words, policy-focused, no ideological framing, no names or parties)

Taxes and benefits
- Raise the personal income tax allowance to £10,000, freeing many low earners from income tax; fund via: basic-rate pension tax relief; aligning capital gains tax with income tax; anti-avoidance; a per-plane duty (with higher domestic rate where alternatives exist); a 1% levy on property value above £2m; time-limit non-domicile status to seven years.
- Restore the state pension link to earnings, uprated by the higher of earnings, prices, or 2.5%.
- Reform tax credits (six‑month fixed awards), end Child Trust Fund payments, and refocus Winter Fuel Payments (extend to severely disabled; defer age-related payments until 65).
- End compulsory annuity purchase at 75; allow limited early pension access; compensate Equitable Life policyholders.

Deficit and spending control
- Identify >£15bn annual savings starting 2011–12; cap public-sector pay rises at £400 for two years; banking levy until retail/investment split complete; scrap ID cards and biometric passport plans; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; prison reform to reduce short sentences; streamline local authority regulation.
- Longer term: no like-for-like replacement of the Trident system; public-sector pension reform; better IT procurement; Council on Financial Stability; emergency budget by June 2010; aim to halve the deficit by 2013–14.

Economy, jobs, banking
- Separate retail and investment banking; reform bonuses; ensure lending to viable firms.
- Create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges.
- One-year green stimulus (~£3.1bn) to create ~100,000 jobs: shipyard refurbishment for offshore renewables; £400 “eco cashback” for home efficiency/microgeneration; energy-efficiency loans for public buildings; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; low‑carbon bus scrappage.
- Youth offer: up to 800,000 work placements; 15,000 Foundation Degree places; boost adult learning support.
- Establish a UK Infrastructure Bank to crowd-in private finance for transport and energy; invest in superfast broadband.
- Reduce red tape; end “gold-plating” of EU rules; reform business rates to site values under local control; refocus/scrap RDAs as locally supported; restore a public-interest test for takeovers; use public procurement for green markets.
- Support mutuals/co‑ops; convert Northern Rock to a building society; reform Royal Mail/Post Office ownership; promote community energy.

Science, work and equality
- Protect the science budget post-CSR; peer‑review funding; publish state‑funded research; support innovative research and tackle gender gaps; safeguard advisers’ independence.
- Extend the right to request flexible working to all; name‑blind applications and pay audits in firms >100 staff; disclose remuneration ≥£200k; strengthen disability employment support.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn “Pupil Premium” for disadvantaged pupils; smaller classes; one‑to‑one and catch‑up tuition; universal SEN assessment at 5; improve teacher training; anti‑bullying measures.
- Independent standards authority; slimmed early years framework; replace National Curriculum with a minimum entitlement; scale back KS2 tests; unified diploma; college options at 14–19; fairer post‑16 funding.
- Limit political micro‑management of schools; local oversight; inclusive admissions in faith schools; flexible pay.
- Phase out tuition fees over six years (final‑year fees scrapped immediately); National Bursary Scheme; merge skills/HE funding bodies; rebalance towards vocational routes; refocus adult skills funding.

Health and care
- Shift funds from bureaucracy to frontline; halve Department of Health; abolish Strategic Health Authorities and some quangos; prioritise prevention; integrate health and social care; guaranteed respite for full‑time carers; prioritise dementia research; expand talking therapies.
- Entitlements for timely diagnosis/treatment (with funded alternatives if missed); frontline staff budget control; elected Local Health Boards; open GP choice and email access; extra GP funding for high‑need areas; neutral commissioning across providers.
- Patient safety transparency; language/competence tests for doctors; measures against A&E violence; support for contaminated blood victims; reduce air pollution; review alcohol pricing/tax to curb binge drinking.

Culture, media, sport, consumers
- Keep free entry to national museums; Creative Enterprise Fund; ease live‑music licensing; reform Lottery tax; invest dormant betting funds in local sport; protect playing fields; sustain BBC independence while avoiding unfair competition; support local media.
- Consumer measures: fair energy tariffs with cheapest initial block and social tariffs; address water charge inequities; cap unfair bank fees; expand basic banking via PostBank; consult on interest caps for credit/store cards; universal service standards; local competition tests for retail; transparent airline pricing; cut regulated rail fares by RPI–1 and compensate for rail‑replacement buses; regulate private clamping.

Environment and energy
- Zero‑carbon economy by 2050; at least 40% UK electricity from non‑carbon sources by 2020 (rising to 100% by 2050), with strong offshore/marine focus; renewables roadmap and European Supergrid.
- Ten‑year home insulation offer (up to £10,000 per home); energy upgrades for schools/public buildings; low‑carbon bus scrappage.
- Block new coal without top‑tier CCS; oppose new nuclear; strengthen energy‑efficiency schemes; 30% energy‑efficiency target by 2020; support EU 30% emissions cut by 2020; tighten EU ETS; zero net deforestation by 2020; ban illegal timber; develop environmental product labelling.

International development and foreign/defence
- Enshrine 0.7% of GNI aid by 2013; explore financial transaction tax and aviation/shipping carbon markets; reform IFIs; tackle corruption and tax havens; fund climate adaptation/mitigation additional to aid; prioritise health, education, gender, water; expand debt relief; act against vulture funds.
- Strategic Security and Defence Review; review procurement; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; no like‑for‑like nuclear replacement; enhance European defence cooperation.
- Improve pay for lower ranks; accelerate family housing upgrades; reduce MoD overheads.
- Use EU cooperation on financial regulation, jobs, crime, agriculture, budget reform; future in/out referendum on fundamental EU changes; any euro entry only by referendum and when conditions are met.
- Foreign policy: coordinated EU engagement on major dossiers; conditions‑based Afghanistan strategy; arms trade controls and broker regulation; diplomatic approach to Iran with targeted sanctions; inquiry into rendition/torture; two‑state approach in the Middle East and end to the Gaza blockade.

Communities, crime, immigration, housing, transport, countryside
- Fund 3,000 additional police; cut police bureaucracy; directly elected police authorities with stronger powers; statutory youth services; create a National Crime Reduction Agency; hospital data‑sharing on violent crime; safer night bus stops; record hate crimes robustly.
- Drugs policy focused on treatment; independent scientific advice.
- Justice: work and victim compensation in prisons; presumption against <6‑month sentences; move addicts/mentally ill to appropriate settings; expand restorative justice and neighbourhood panels; cancel new prison build.
- Immigration: reinstate exit checks; create a National Border Force; regional points‑based work system; toughen employer checks; prioritise deportations of serious offenders; earned citizenship for long‑term, law‑abiding residents present before 2010.
- Asylum: independent agency; EU‑wide coordination; right to work; end child detention; alternatives to detention; no returns to danger.
- Housing: repossession as last resort; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; national insulation; raise building standards; enable councils to build and retain revenues; scrap HIPs, retain EPCs.
- Transport: invest in local rail and high‑speed rail via UKIB; regulate buses locally; safer cycling/walking; replace per‑passenger air duty with per‑plane duty (higher domestic where alternatives exist); cancel Heathrow third runway and other SE expansions; prepare revenue‑neutral road pricing; rural fuel discount; target zero‑emission new cars by 2040.
- Natural environment: expand access; localised planning with third‑party appeal; zero‑waste strategy and product durability standards; biodiversity recovery by 2020; equalise VAT on repair/new build; elected National Park members; protect local green spaces; double woodland by 2050; stop “garden grabbing”; flood‑risk controls; smart water metering; restore wetlands.
- Rural communities and farming: higher council tax or planning controls on second homes where needed; sustain post offices via PostBank; promote affordable rural housing; VAT refund to mountain rescue; create a Supermarket Code and regulator; retarget Single Farm Payments toward working/smaller farms and uplands; support farm biogas and apprenticeships; CAP reform toward environment; clearer origin/environmental labelling; green and fair‑trade public procurement.

Political and constitutional reform, civil liberties
- Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and fewer MPs; votes at 16; fixed‑term parliaments; stronger Commons budget and appointments scrutiny; fully elected second chamber; written constitution via citizens’ convention and referendum; strengthen data protection; extend FOI to monopoly public services.
- Clean politics: recall for serious wrongdoing; cap donations at £10,000; tax‑residency requirements for MPs/Lords/candidates; statutory lobbyist register, tighter ministerial code, corporate lobbying disclosures, candidate interest register.
- Decentralisation: fair votes for local elections; pilot local income tax; return business rates to councils on site values; review local finance; elected health boards and police authorities; scrap various regional bodies and central inspections; implement community sustainability rights.
- Devolution: new powers for Scotland and Wales; needs‑based funding formula; address England’s status; resolve specified Scottish revenue issues.
- Civil liberties: Freedom Bill (CCTV regulation; stop surveillance abuses; protect jury trials and protest rights); scrap ID cards and related databases; halt unnecessary offences; curb communications data retention; remove innocent DNA; protect the Human Rights Act; enable intercept evidence; reduce pre‑charge detention to 14 days; scrap control orders; community‑led counter‑radicalisation.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_C" | "TEXT_D"
}
